linkedin-late-response.description: Polite LinkedIn message template for responding to a recruiter outreach after a delay. The placeholders should be filled with the recruiter's name and the company name. Useful for quickly replying to recruiter messages when you haven't checked LinkedIn in a while, while expressing interest and asking about compensation to determine if it's worth pursuing further.
body: Hi ${1:recruiter name}, thanks for reaching out! Sorry for the delayed response, I don't check LinkedIn very frequently, but I'd be very interested to explore further with ${2:company name}. Do you have information about expected compensation range? If that aligns, I can move quickly as well.

email-reject-small-company.description: Polite email template for rejecting a recruiter outreach from a small company when you're not actively looking. The placeholder should be filled with the recruiter's name and the company name. Useful for maintaining good relationships while setting clear boundaries about your current job search status.
body: Thanks for reaching out, but I'm currently only passively searching for later stage opportunities, I'm quite busy with my own business at the moment so I couldn't explore further with ${2:company name}.

email-good-product.description: Polite email template for expressing interest in a company with an attractive product, while probing for compensation and remote work flexibility. The placeholders should be filled with the recruiter's name and the company name. Useful for quickly responding to recruiter outreach when the product is appealing but you need more information to determine if it's worth pursuing.
body: I'm quite interested and aligned with the product at ${2:company name}, do you have any information on potential compensation and remote friendliness? I have an injury which makes it difficult to commute, but if remote is possible and compensation can compare with my current role at Apollo I'd love to explore.

email-probe-remote.description: Polite email template for probing whether a non-remote or hybrid role has flexibility for fully remote, based on current experience at Pocus. The placeholder should be filled with the recruiter's name.
body: Thanks for reaching out, would there be flexibility for a fully remote configuration? That's how I've learned to operate here at Pocus and it'd be pretty difficult to let that style go.

email-role-preferences.description: Canned response describing ideal role criteria for recruiter conversations: large org for learning, fully remote preferred, nights/weekends free for personal business, hybrid only for exceptional offers. Useful as a quick paste when a recruiter asks what you're looking for.
body: Ideally, I'm looking for somewhere that I can learn from a large organization's engineering practices while maintaining time at night and weekends to work on my own business. Due to family constraints, especially in the future, it should be fully remote. But for the right offer, I could flex hybrid if absolutely necessary.$0

empty-tasks.description: Scaffold a full tasks section with lifecycle categories: todo for uncommitted work, ongoing (active/passive/waiting) for in-flight items with different attention levels, done for completed work, and cancelled for abandoned items. Use this at the top of any project or session markdown file to establish a task tracking structure.
